items.title: UK Budget sets a Data Centre Covenant: 6 GW of AI data centre capacity needed by 2030, with grid capacity reserved for strategic sites that sign up
items.summary: HM Treasury published the Data Centre Covenant with the Autumn Budget on 28 October 2026. The government estimates the UK needs 6 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2030 so it is not reliant almost entirely on overseas compute. Strategic data centres that want enhanced support must meet tests: credible commitments for the grid capacity they request, a Local Benefit Plan scaled to project size, a Power Usage Effectiveness of 1.3 or better with annual energy and water reporting, local jobs and apprenticeships with a contribution to British AI hardware, and secure access to compute for the NHS and public services. In return, ministers will use Planning and Infrastructure Act powers to reserve and reallocate grid capacity, allow transfer of pre-2030 connection contracts and, in narrow cases, temporary on-site generation. The Budget also adds £140 million for the Sovereign AI Unit. Caveat: which sites count as strategic and the full criteria are still to be published, and a draft National Policy Statement goes to consultation. Country conversion: the UK trades grid priority for local and security commitments.
items.source: HM Treasury, The Data Centre Covenant, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); New Civil Engineer 29 Oct 2026

items.title: L&T's Vyoma.AI breaks ground on a 52 MW liquid-cooled AI data centre at its Chennai AI Factory campus
items.summary: Larsen & Toubro said on 28 October 2026 that Vyoma.AI, its AI cloud and hyperscale data centre business, held the groundbreaking for a 52 MW AI-ready data centre in Chennai with direct-to-chip liquid cooling, aimed at hyperscalers, neoclouds and AI developers. It sits on L&T's planned gigawatt-scale AI Factory campus in Chennai, which already runs AI compute clusters in an operational 30 MW facility and has 150 MVA of power infrastructure ready. Vyoma targets over 250 MW across India. Caveat: no completion date, tenant or cost disclosed. Country conversion: Chennai adds another domestic-owned AI build days after OneQode's 14 MW at AdaniConneX.
items.source: Larsen & Toubro press release, 28 Oct 2026 (primary); The Hindu

items.title: Brazil's 5G auction fund approves a R$375 million sovereign AI data centre for the federal government, run by Telebras
items.summary: Gaispi, the group that directs projects funded by Brazil's 5G spectrum auction through the entity EAF, approved on 27 October 2026 a sovereign data centre for federal government AI projects at an estimated R$375 million, according to IA News citing Teletime and Convergência Digital. The AI module would have 20 racks, six GPU servers with 48 GPUs in total, nine CPU servers and liquid cooling, plus a separate colocation module of up to ten racks. The facility would be federally owned and operated by Telebras, with deployment estimated at 12 months depending on power, licensing and equipment delivery. Caveat: still needs approval from Anatel's board; GPU model not disclosed. Country conversion: Brazil funds a small first sovereign AI cluster from money already collected.
items.source: IA News 29 Oct 2026, citing Teletime and Convergência Digital

items.title: Seychelles Cabinet approves a sovereign government cloud on two in-country datacentres and a 2026 to 2031 Digital and AI Strategy
items.summary: State House said Cabinet, chaired by Vice-President Sebastien Pillay on 28 October 2026, approved the Seychelles Digital and AI Strategy 2026 to 2031 and the Government Cloud and Datacenter Project: a sovereign, in-country government cloud on two geographically separated datacentres, meant to reduce reliance on commercial and overseas infrastructure and provide local cloud and AI computing. Phase 1 builds the cloud and primary datacentre; Phase 2 adds the secondary site and expands cloud and AI capability. Caveat: no budget, capacity, vendor or timeline disclosed. Country conversion: a small island state moves government workloads onshore.
items.source: State House Seychelles, Cabinet Business 28 Oct 2026 (primary); Seychelles News Agency

items.title: Korea will trim AI data centre power demand in its 12th power plan to confirmed projects only, two months after lifting the forecast to 11.9 GW
items.summary: Climate, Energy and Environment Minister Kim Sung-hwan told a National Assembly audit on 26 October 2026 that only confirmed AI data centre demand will go into the 12th Basic Plan for Long-term Electricity Supply and Demand, saying that once the three mega-projects began, 'not much demand has actually been firmed up in concrete terms'. In August the ministry had raised projected 2040 AIDC peak demand to 11.9 GW from 4 GW against an 18.4 GW by 2035 build plan (SK, GS and Naver 8.4 GW by 2029). GS has started a 1.2 GW first phase in Donghae for 2028; SK has not detailed its 4 GW of regional sites beyond the 100 MW Ulsan build with AWS. AI-DC Korea counts 522 projects (3.4 GW) in grid impact review as of Q1, of which 10 (1 GW) have secured power. The science ministry said on 27 October the mega-projects remain on track. Caveat: no reduction figure set; plan goes to the Assembly in late December or early January. Country conversion: Korea's grid planner is discounting announced gigawatts to what has firm demand.
items.source: Seoul Economic Daily 27 Oct 2026 (minister at parliamentary audit); MSIT explanatory note 27 Oct 2026

items.title: OneQode signs 14 MW of AI capacity with AdaniConneX in Chennai, in talks for up to 114 MW in India
items.summary: Singapore-based OneQode said on 27 October 2026 (US Eastern; 28 October in India) it signed an agreement with AdaniConneX for 14 MW of data centre capacity at Siruseri SIPCOT, Chennai, its first major AI deployment in India, for training, inference, enterprise and sovereign workloads. The companies are discussing additional capacity of up to 114 MW, which OneQode says could generate over $6 billion of GPU-as-a-service total contract value. The build uses AMD Instinct GPUs under a May 2026 collaboration, with AMD Helios racks planned. It follows CoreWeave's 240 MW plan at AdaniConneX Navi Mumbai earlier this month. Caveat: only the 14 MW is signed; the 114 MW and $6 billion figures are company targets. Country conversion: a second foreign GPU cloud takes Indian colocation for regional inference.
items.source: OneQode press release via PR Newswire, 27 Oct 2026 (primary)

items.title: Switzerland tenders the Swiss Government Cloud: up to CHF 7 billion over 14 years in three lots, one lot per bidder
items.summary: The Federal Office of Information Technology, Systems and Telecommunication published the Swiss Government Cloud tender (WTO 25002 609) on SIMAP on 20 October 2026. Lot 1 is global public cloud (two awards, up to CHF 2 billion), lot 2 is public cloud with data stored and processed only in Switzerland on open source (two awards, up to CHF 2 billion), and lot 3 is private cloud in federal data centres (one award, up to CHF 3 billion). No bidder can win more than one lot; awards run seven years and re-open, for 14 years in total, and spending is pay as you use. Prequalification runs 60 days; awards are expected late summer 2027 and first call-offs late autumn 2027. Caveat: CHF 7 billion is a ceiling, not a commitment. Country conversion: Switzerland caps any one provider's share of federal cloud by design.
items.source: Federal Department of Finance / FOITT press release, 20 Oct 2026 (primary)

items.title: Bull and CRA sign MoU for the Czech AI Gigafactory bid, first deal under the France-Czech AI pact
items.summary: Bull and Ceske Radiokomunikace (CRA) said on 21 October 2026 they signed a strategic memorandum to combine CRA's infrastructure with Bull's systems, software and services in the CRA-led consortium bidding for the Czech AI Gigafactory (AIGF CZ) under the EU AI Gigafactories programme. It is the first industrial agreement under the bilateral AI and digital cooperation agreement signed by French minister Anne Le Henanff and Czech minister Karel Havlicek. Bull says its Czech and French manufacturing with Foxconn could build the servers, and it plans to reserve capacity for its own clients. CRA runs eight data centres and already sells GPU capacity. Caveat: non-binding; capacity, site, chips and cost not disclosed, and the EU selection is pending. Country conversion: Czechia positions a telco-led bid as the Central and Eastern European gigafactory candidate.
items.source: Bull press release, 21 Oct 2026 (primary); CRA press release

items.title: Crusoe takes Polar's 40 MW DRA02 building at Tørdal, Norway, for Vera Rubin NVL72; DRA01 live at 12 MW
items.summary: Polar Data Centers said on 21 October 2026 that DRA01 at its hydro-powered Tørdal campus in Norway is live with 12 MW of IT capacity running Crusoe Cloud, and that Crusoe will take DRA02, a second liquid-cooled building of 40 MW critical IT expected live in late 2027, where Crusoe plans to deploy Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72. Caveat: GPU count and contract value not disclosed. Country conversion: Norway's hydro campuses keep converting into US neocloud capacity, now on the Rubin generation.

items.title: Oman signs Yamna to build a large AI data centre in Salalah; first phase over £1 billion
items.summary: The UK government said on 21 October 2026, during Sultan Haitham bin Tarik's state visit, that UK-founded Yamna would sign an agreement with Oman to build a large-scale AI data centre in Salalah, with a first phase expected to exceed £1 billion. Yamna said it signed a strategic cooperation agreement with Oman's Ministry of Transport, Communications and Information Technology for the project, branded Salalah Al Khadra Digital. UK Export Finance raised its capacity for UK exports to Oman to up to £7 billion. Caveat: MoU stage; MW, power source, tenant and chips not disclosed. Country conversion: Oman enters the Gulf AI campus race with a southern site away from the Gulf states' existing hubs.

items.title: G42's Khazna and Core42 sign MoUs with Copelouzos to explore an AI factory in Greece
items.summary: Copelouzos Group said it signed memoranda of understanding in Athens on 22 October 2026 with G42 portfolio companies Khazna Data Centers, which would lead the physical build, and Core42, which would provide cloud and AI compute for banking, telecoms, shipping and public administration, during a UAE Ministry of Foreign Trade business mission. Copelouzos is also developing GREGY, a 3,000 MW Egypt-Greece power interconnector. Caveat: exploratory; scope, site, capacity, financing and timelines are to be defined, subject to definitive agreements and approvals. Country conversion: Greece gets its first Gulf-operator AI factory proposal, tied to an energy group.
items.source: Copelouzos Group press release via Zawya, 22 Oct 2026 (primary)

items.title: Naver signs up to $9 billion Brookfield compute deal, clearing Nvidia's $1 billion equity investment; 55 MW in 1H 2027, 200 MW by 2028
items.summary: Naver said on 27 October 2026 it signed a contract with Brookfield to secure up to $9 billion of AI computing infrastructure. Brookfield will fund a special purpose vehicle, Asset Co., 100% to buy GPUs and data centre capacity; it will be consolidated as a Naver subsidiary under K-IFRS. Naver Cloud operates the capacity and pays usage fees linked to business revenue instead of buying the hardware, and Naver guarantees those payments for up to 8 years. The deal satisfies the condition Naver set for Nvidia's planned $1 billion strategic equity investment (about 1.5 trillion won), which now moves to a third-party paid-in capital increase. The AI Factory hub is the Gak Sejong data centre, with 55 MW in the first half of 2027, 200 MW by 2028 and a long-term 1 GW global goal. Caveat: capital increase terms not yet announced. Country conversion: Korea's largest platform company gets financed sovereign-scale GPU capacity without putting it on its own capex line.
items.source: Digital Today 27 Oct 2026, quoting Naver statement

items.title: Anwar says SoftBank's Son plans $50 billion of AI and data centre investment in Malaysia, with sites in Kuching, Sarawak and the peninsula
items.summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on 24 October 2026 that SoftBank Group chairman Masayoshi Son had identified locations in Kuching, Sarawak and peninsular Malaysia for planned investments of $50 billion in AI, new technologies and data centres, after a video call earlier that week (Bloomberg via CNBC). Sarawak Premier Abang Johari confirmed on 26 October that the plan includes an AI data centre at Tanjung Embang. Earlier in October SoftBank signed a framework with Grab and Petroleum Sarawak Berhad to explore AI and digital infrastructure in Sarawak. Malaysia recorded RM385.7 billion ($94 billion) of data centre related investment from 2021 to 1H 2026 (MIDA). Caveat: SoftBank had not commented; no MW, timeline or binding agreement disclosed. Country conversion: Malaysia's pipeline moves beyond Johor toward Sarawak hydropower.
items.source: CNBC citing Bloomberg, 26 Oct 2026; Malay Mail and The Star, 26 Oct 2026 (Sarawak Premier)

items.title: Crusoe and Araico plan an AI cloud site at Paraguay's Itaipú substation: initial capacity mid-2027, path to 106 MW, options to about 280 MW
items.summary: Crusoe announced on 22 October 2026 a partnership with Paraguayan developer Araico to build AI compute next to the Itaipú substation, powered by the Itaipú hydroelectric dam. An initial deployment is planned for mid-2027 with a path to 106 MW of IT capacity and long-term options to about 280 MW. Araico leads site development; Crusoe operates the compute for Crusoe Cloud, serving US and Latin American customers. It is Crusoe's first AI cloud deployment in Latin America. President Santiago Peña backed it, and US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau, present at signing, said it could be the largest private foreign investment in Paraguay's history. Caveat: no capex figure or GPU count disclosed. Country conversion: Paraguay's surplus Itaipú hydro gets its first named neocloud tenant.

items.title: CoreWeave brings most of 22.5 MW online at atNorth DEN01 in Copenhagen and extends its network backbone to seven Middle East and Asia Pacific markets
items.summary: CoreWeave said on 27 October 2026 it has brought the majority of a planned 22.5 MW of IT capacity online at atNorth's DEN01 in Copenhagen, its first Denmark deployment, running NVIDIA Blackwell systems on Quantum-X800 InfiniBand, with surplus heat going to district heating. Its European footprint is now nine data centres in five geographies including the UK, Spain, Sweden and Norway. It is also adding network points of presence in the UAE, India, Indonesia, Singapore, Australia, Korea and Japan from late Q4 2026, closing a four-continent loop by mid-2027. Caveat: points of presence are network, not GPU capacity. Country conversion: Denmark gets live neocloud GPU capacity days after its grid priority order on data centres.

items.title: Freedom Holding advances Kazakhstan's $2 billion Sovereign AI Hub: 100 MW site, first public GPU cloud in 2027
items.summary: Freedom Holding said on 26 October 2026 it is advancing a $2 billion Sovereign AI Hub under a November 2025 agreement with Kazakhstan's Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development, on a site with 100 MW of available power, with Freedom as principal financing partner and operator. Its first GPU cluster will open as a public cloud in 2027, and the first phase of a Freedom AI Super Cluster is planned for Q1 2027; a Freedom Cloud data centre is under construction near Almaty. CEO Timur Turlov says demand is twice first-stage capacity and prospective clients will lease for five years. Caveat: GPU count, vendor and exact site not disclosed. Country conversion: Kazakhstan adds a domestic, financed sovereign GPU cloud alongside the Firebird export-licensed build.
items.source: Freedom Holding Corp. press release, 26 Oct 2026 (primary)

items.title: Anthropic's public S-1 puts numbers on its US compute rent: up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI, $125.2 billion Broadcom TPU lease, $44.6 billion Nscale, $41.3 billion Lambda
items.summary: Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly on 26 October 2026. The filing says it agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI for NVIDIA GPU compute over terms into 2029, about $3.1 billion a month once all capacity is delivered (expected December 2026), cancellable on 90 days' notice after initial non-cancelable periods ending January and March 2027. A five-year Broadcom equipment lease for AI accelerators carries about $125.2 billion of rent excluding interest and is non-cancelable except on default; Anthropic may issue up to $42.0 billion of convertible notes to Broadcom to finance it. Nscale agreements total up to about $44.6 billion into 2033 and Lambda agreements about $41.3 billion into 2034; both accrue fees only on delivery, Nscale must use best efforts to obtain financing, and about $34.9 billion of the Lambda total can be terminated if Lambda does not secure the facility lease. First-half 2026 revenue was $16.3 billion and operating loss $693 million. Caveat: the filing leaves the total commitment figure blank; third-party totals (Yahoo Finance about $430 billion non-cancelable) are estimates. Country conversion: the largest single disclosed book of rented compute, mostly sited in the US, now has public terms.
items.source: Anthropic S-1, SEC EDGAR, 26 Oct 2026 (primary); Yahoo Finance 26 Oct 2026

items.title: Meta launches a $95 billion equity financing plan for AI infrastructure: $35 billion underwritten now, $60 billion at-the-market from Q1 2027
items.summary: Meta announced concurrent underwritten offerings of about $22.5 billion of Class A common stock (via forward sale agreements) and about $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred depositary shares, plus a planned $60 billion at-the-market program in non-voting Class C stock that is not expected to start before Q1 2027. NVIDIA, AMD and Broadcom indicated non-binding interest in buying up to $5.0 billion of the Class A shares. Meta reiterated 2026 capex of $135 to $145 billion, said it owns data centers in 23 US states, is building four superclusters of more than 1 GW each and is on track to nearly double infrastructure capacity in 2026. It generated $97 billion of operating cash flow in the first three quarters and held about $82 billion of cash and securities. Caveat: the ATM program has no signed agreement and its timing, size and terms are not set. Country conversion: a US hyperscaler is now funding its compute build with new equity, not only cash flow and debt.
items.source: Meta investor release 26 Oct 2026 (primary); CNBC 26 Oct 2026

items.title: SpaceX signs binding commitment for an Apollo-managed master finance lease covering about $40 billion of GPU pods
items.summary: SpaceX's 8-K (filed 26 October 2026) says that on 24 October it entered a binding commitment letter for a master finance lease under which an Apollo-managed entity will buy and lease GPU pods and related equipment for data centers SpaceX selects. Tranches carry lease terms of about five to five and a quarter years, rent is quarterly in advance at one-twentieth of financed cost plus a fixed rate set at pricing, and aggregate principal payments are expected to total about $40 billion. Closing is expected before year end, with lease schedules starting in the first half of 2027 as GPUs arrive. Elon Musk posted that the deal had closed and that debt markets have almost entirely shut for companies without substantial non-data-center revenue. Caveat: the filing describes a commitment subject to closing conditions, not a closed financing, and does not name the GPU model or sites. Country conversion: US GPU capacity financed against an investment-grade, non-AI revenue base.
items.source: SpaceX 8-K, SEC EDGAR, 26 Oct 2026 (primary); CNBC 25 and 26 Oct 2026

items.title: SK Hyper seeks about $350 billion for the first 5 GW of a 15 GW South Korean AI data center plan by 2035
items.summary: SK Hyper CEO Chung Suk-keun told Bloomberg TV on 23 October 2026 that the SK Telecom unit is in talks with big tech companies and financial investors to fund 15 GW of data center capacity in South Korea by 2035, and that the first 5 GW phase alone would need about $350 billion (about 463 trillion won) including servers and equipment. It targets a first outside round by end 2026 or early 2027, plans phased operations from 2029, and starts with a 900 MW Ulsan project alongside a 100 MW AWS facility, aiming for a 2 GW plus Yeongnam cluster and further GW sites in Chungcheong and the southwest. Chung put Korea's current data center market at about 1 GW and said the plan depends on drawing inference and training demand from Japan, Taiwan and other Asian markets. SK Telecom plans to invest up to 750 billion won in SK Hyper through 2030. Caveat: an estimate for a financing-dependent plan; no investor, term sheet or customer has been named, and the pace will follow demand.
items.source: Bloomberg TV 23 Oct 2026; Seoul Economic Daily 23 Oct 2026; Business Times 23 Oct 2026; Hankyung 23 Oct 2026

items.title: Texas environmental regulator suspends at least 17 data center construction stormwater and wastewater authorizations and shuts its online permit portal
items.summary: After Public Citizen and FracTracker reported that automated approvals kept flowing despite Governor Greg Abbott's pause on data center permits, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality suspended at least 17 stormwater and wastewater authorizations tied to data center projects and closed its online application system; applications must now be filed physically. TCEQ says all data-center-related notices of intent are suspended and that these automated notices do not authorize operation, though they are required before clearing land of an acre or more. The governor's office says no state agency will approve data center permits until the PUC, ERCOT and the Water Development Board have the information they need. Caveat: the count of 17 comes from the watchdog groups; TCEQ and the governor's office dispute that any permit was improperly approved. Country conversion: the largest US build state has paused the paperwork that starts construction.
items.source: Houston Public Media 22 Oct 2026; Texas Tribune 21 Oct 2026; Tom's Hardware

items.title: UK Treasury previews Budget AI package: extra £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund and £18 million for an Advanced Chip Design Academy
items.summary: HM Treasury said on 24 October 2026 that the Chancellor will make AI part of next week's Budget, including an additional £60 million for the Sovereign AI Fund to invest directly in UK AI companies (adding Physical and Industrial AI), a further £60 million for Sovereign AI's R&D Procurement Scheme, £18 million for a new UK Advanced Chip Design Academy, AI chip design capability in Edinburgh, an AI Centre of Excellence in Manchester and £10 million a year to study AI's effect on jobs. Caveat: these are announced allocations ahead of the Budget, not compute capacity, and no data center, power or GPU figures were given. Country conversion: small sovereign capital, aimed at chip design and firms rather than megawatts, a week after Microsoft left Nscale's Loughton site over grid delays.

items.title: Kazakhstan signs Firebird investment agreement as Firebird secures a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs
items.summary: During Jensen Huang's first visit to Astana on 23 October 2026, Firebird signed an investment agreement with the government of Kazakhstan at the Akorda presidential palace. NVIDIA says Firebird has secured a US export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs; the first phase is under construction with Kazakhtelecom at Data Center Valley in Ekibastuz, targeting commercial launch in Q3 2027, and a planned second phase would take Firebird's potential capacity in Kazakhstan to about 500 MW. Kazakhtelecom has already deployed 400 H200 and 480 B300 GPUs in Astana and Almaty and plans more than 1,000 GPUs at Data Center Valley plus more than 1,000 Vera Rubin GPUs in the Ekibastuz region in 2027. NVIDIA also announced an investment in Kazakhstan-founded Higgsfield AI. Huang called the country a future 'AI factory hub for all of Europe' (CNBC). Caveat: no contract value, power source or financing was disclosed, and the second phase is planned, not committed. Country conversion: a named US export license turns Kazakhstan's Ekibastuz plan into licensed GPU supply.
items.source: NVIDIA blog 22 Oct 2026 (primary); Astana Times 23 Oct 2026; CNBC 23 Oct 2026

items.title: Amazon drops data centers on its $427 million GW campus in Loudoun County after resident opposition
items.summary: Loudoun County's Board of Supervisors voted unanimously on 20 October 2026 for a preliminary agreement ('Project Potomac Promise') that is intended to eliminate data center uses on the George Washington University Virginia Science and Technology Campus in Ashburn, which AWS bought earlier in 2026 (reported at $427 million for 122 acres). Amazon will convey about 25 acres worth about $65 million to the county, donate $5 million to the housing trust fund, withdraw its data center application and forgo legal action; the county will fast-track rezoning of the remaining 97 acres for housing and mixed use. The county says Amazon acknowledged significant opposition to data centers at the site. Final agreements are still to be negotiated, and one supervisor voted against fast-tracking the rezoning. Separately, the board deferred to 17 November a resolution to pause data center and substation legislative applications for up to 12 months. Country conversion: in the world's largest data center market, a hyperscaler has given up an owned site rather than fight local opposition.
items.source: Loudoun County news release 22 Oct 2026 (primary); WTOP 21 Oct 2026; Washington Post 22 Oct 2026

items.title: ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent reportedly order more than 3 million export-compliant NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500 cards worth over $35 billion
items.summary: Reuters reported on 20 October 2026, citing two people familiar with the matter, that ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent have ordered more than 3 million NVIDIA RTX PRO 5500 cards at about $11,400 each, a combined sticker value of more than $35 billion, mainly for inference. The sources say total orders from Chinese customers exceed 6 million, that NVIDIA told customers it cannot guarantee delivery, that partners may receive only 5% to 10% of requested quantities, and that NVIDIA indicated it could make no more than 3 million cards globally in 2027 as TSMC capacity shifts to Rubin. Samples are expected in December with commercial deliveries from Q1 2027. B300 cannot be sold to Chinese buyers and H200 exports are licensed case by case. An NVIDIA spokesperson blamed outdated US export controls and China's own import limits; the three buyers did not comment. Caveat: single outlet, anonymous sources, orders are not deliveries. Country conversion: China's demand for compliant NVIDIA inference silicon is about twice the stated global supply.

items.title: IREN secures grid power and a civil works license for a planned 300 MW AI campus in Badajoz, Spain, targeting 2028
items.summary: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin on 21 October 2026, IREN announced it has secured grid-connected power and the civil works license for a planned AI data center of about 300 MW in Badajoz, Extremadura, with initial operations targeted for 2028. The campus uses closed-loop liquid cooling, is designed for NVIDIA DSX compatibility, and will offer managed AI cloud services for customers with data residency requirements. IREN also set up IREN Europe, chaired by former Banco Santander CEO Angel Corcostegui, with Roberto Purcaro as Executive Director for Europe. IREN entered Spain in June 2026 by buying developer Nostrum Group. Europa Press reports construction should start between late 2026 and early 2027. No customer, capex or GPU count was disclosed. Country conversion: Spain gets a permitted, grid-connected 300 MW neocloud site while UK projects stall on grid queues.
items.source: IREN release 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Europa Press 21 Oct 2026

items.title: Humain and NVIDIA plan up to 84 MW and about 27,000 GPUs in Saudi Arabia, including 50 MW of Vera Rubin for an unnamed US client
items.summary: At NVIDIA GTC Berlin on 22 October 2026, Humain (PIF-owned) and NVIDIA announced an expanded collaboration covering a multi-phase rollout of up to 84 MW of AI compute in Saudi Arabia, about 27,000 GPUs. Phase one is 14 MW of NVIDIA Blackwell HGX B300 systems, about 6,000 GPUs on Quantum-X800 InfiniBand, with deployment starting in Q4 2026 for Humain Cloud customers. Humain then expects 70 MW of Vera Rubin infrastructure, about 21,000 GPUs, from June 2027: 50 MW for frontier-scale workloads of an unnamed US-based client and 20 MW for Humain Cloud from July or August 2027, all on the NVIDIA DSX platform. The National reports the Vera Rubin phases remain subject to final agreements. Humain targets nearly 3 GW of data center capacity by 2030 and more than 6 GW by 2034. Caveat: no primary release URL was found at our cutoff; figures are from The National and Data Centre Magazine, which quote both companies. Country conversion: a second named offtake for Saudi export compute in two days, after Nebius at Oxagon.
items.source: The National 22 Oct 2026; Data Centre Magazine 22 Oct 2026 (company quotes)

items.title: Google and Voltus expand to a 1 GW Google-funded virtual power plant across PJM
items.summary: On 22 October 2026 Google and Voltus announced an expanded agreement to build a 1 GW virtual power plant across the PJM region (13 states plus Washington, D.C., about 67 million people). Voltus aggregates flexible demand from businesses and homes, such as smart thermostats, batteries and industrial assets, that cut use during peaks; Google funds it and participants receive bill savings and cash payments. It is a tenfold expansion of a 100 MW agreement from earlier in 2026, and Google calls it one of the largest distributed capacity portfolios deployed by a hyperscaler. The release gives no cost, timeline or link to specific Google campuses. Country conversion: in the tightest US capacity market, a hyperscaler is buying demand response at gigawatt scale to make room for its own load.

items.title: UK industry taskforce with NVIDIA, Microsoft and Cisco tells ministers they have about 12 months to win local consent for data centres
items.summary: The Guardian reported on 22 October 2026 (exclusive) that the Sovereign AI Leadership (SAIL) taskforce, whose members include NVIDIA, Microsoft and Cisco, told the UK government it has a window of roughly 12 months to build a compact that earns public consent before US-style organised opposition takes hold. The submission asks for a national framework of recommended local-benefit terms for councils and mayors, including an indicative contribution scaled to site size, and for host councils to keep more business rates. It cites dry summers and rising energy bills as drivers of scrutiny. Action to Protect Rural Scotland says 15 community campaigns are already active in Scotland. A government spokesperson pointed to existing measures letting councils in England's AI growth zones keep all additional business rates. Caveat: single outlet; the submission itself was not published. Country conversion: the industry is asking Britain to pay for social licence before the build-out, after Microsoft's Loughton exit and NextDC's consent-driven delay.

items.title: South Korea's chip exports hit a record US$27.5 billion for 1 to 20 October, up 222.5%, 44.7% of all exports
items.summary: Preliminary Korea Customs Service data released on 21 October 2026 show South Korea's total exports for 1 to 20 October at US$61.6 billion, up 105.4% year on year and a record for the period. Semiconductor exports rose 222.5% to US$27.5 billion and made up 44.7% of total exports, up 16.2 percentage points from a year earlier; computer peripherals rose 424.0%. Imports rose 42.8% to US$47.1 billion. The data are preliminary. Working-day-adjusted daily exports rose 65.9%, so part of the headline jump reflects more working days than in the same period of 2025. Country conversion: memory and AI server pricing is now the main driver of Korea's trade account, days before SK hynix (28 Oct) and Samsung (29 Oct) report.
items.source: Korea Customs Service via Korea.kr briefing 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Yonhap 21 Oct 2026

items.title: NextDC cuts FY27 guidance and pauses all uncontracted development after Jemena suspends grid works for M3 Melbourne; shares fall about 42%
items.summary: On 21 October 2026 NextDC ended its trading halt with an ASX release saying Jemena Electricity Networks suspended parts of the 66 kV line works needed for the next increase in grid supply to its M3 Melbourne (West Footscray) data centre, citing safety concerns, community and stakeholder opposition and the lack of local council consent. Jemena does not expect to restart before February 2027, and NextDC now expects that supply increase in FY28. Later increases also depend on new transformers at the Brooklyn Terminal Station, which are now expected later than planned. The Victorian planning decision on M3 Stages 6 and 7 is not expected until 2027 because of the 28 November state election. NextDC removed the affected M3 contracts, about A$140 million each of net revenue and underlying EBITDA, from FY27 guidance: net revenue A$475 to 500 million (was A$615 to 640 million), underlying EBITDA A$245 to 265 million (was A$385 to 410 million), capex A$4.5 to 5.0 billion (was A$5.25 to 5.75 billion). All new development projects and land acquisitions are on hold, site sales will be evaluated, and the contracts allow service level credits and in some cases termination; NextDC is assessing force majeure relief. Liquidity was A$8.675 billion at 30 September and covenants are met. Reuters reports the shares closed down 41.7%, about A$3 billion of market value, the worst day since listing in 2010. Country conversion: contracted Australian hyperscale capacity stalls on distribution-network works blocked by local opposition.
items.source: NextDC ASX release 21 Oct 2026 (primary); Reuters 21 Oct 2026; ABC News 21 Oct 2026

items.title: Humain and DataVolt sign a preliminary framework with Nebius for up to 50 MW at the Oxagon AI campus in NEOM, Saudi Arabia
items.summary: On 21 October 2026 Humain (PIF) and DataVolt announced a preliminary framework agreement with Nebius for capacity at their planned AI giga campus in Oxagon, NEOM. Nebius would be the anchor customer, with a contemplated offtake of up to 50 MW, half of the first 100 MW now under construction within a planned 360 MW first phase. The capacity is expected to come online in phases from Q4 2027, and Nebius expects to deploy NVIDIA-based infrastructure. The release says construction began about six weeks earlier; the agreement was signed on the sidelines of NVIDIA GTC Berlin. The framework is preliminary and the release gives no contract value or term. Country conversion: the first named international offtaker for a Saudi build-to-export AI campus.
items.source: NEOM / Humain / DataVolt joint release 21 Oct 2026 (primary)

items.title: Wisconsin DNR settles the Vantage Port Washington permit case by agreeing to a statewide data center strategic analysis due January 2028
items.summary: On 19 October 2026 the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources, Sierra Club and Midwest Environmental Advocates announced a settlement (signed 16 October) of the challenge to DNR permits for Vantage's Port Washington data center campus. The permits stay valid and the case is dismissed. In return DNR will complete a statewide Data Center Strategic Analysis by 31 January 2028 covering AI data center buildout, related energy infrastructure, alternatives and cumulative environmental effects, with public scoping and hearings; Vantage pays the preparation costs and DNR keeps control of the analysis. Wisconsin Examiner reports DNR will also prepare full environmental impact statements for individual data center proposals going forward. A state PSC report this summer found Port Washington plus Microsoft's Mount Pleasant and Meta's Beaver Dam campuses set to drive a 40% rise in statewide energy demand over six years. Country conversion: a US state adds a statewide review layer for future campuses without stopping the one under construction.
items.source: Midwest Environmental Advocates release and settlement filing 16 to 19 Oct 2026 (primary); Wisconsin Examiner 19 Oct 2026; WPR

items.title: Entergy Arkansas adds a second phase of service for Google's West Memphis campus, with Google paying for about $600 million of grid investment, a 440 MW solar PPA and 1,400 MWh of batteries
items.summary: On 19 October 2026 Entergy Arkansas announced a second phase of service for Google's data center campus in West Memphis, Arkansas, which it says will fulfill Google's plan for data center buildings on the site and accelerate the ramp of the original project. Google will cover about $600 million of planned investment plus a power purchase agreement: a 1,000 MWh battery at Driver Solar near Osceola and a 400 MWh battery near Hot Springs (both expected online in 2028), a 440 MW (ac) solar PPA for the Big Island facility in Mississippi County, an expansion of the Galet substation and two new 230 kV lines to serve the expanded campus. The Big Island PPA was added after Arkansas PSC guidance; the commission had denied Entergy's earlier request to take that plant's output in September. Entergy says Google pays the full cost of the resources for its service over a 20-year contract and projects at least $500 million in new customer savings from 2028, on top of $1.6 billion from phase 1. The expansion still needs Arkansas PSC approval; expected in-service date is 2028. DCD puts the campus at 600 MW. Country conversion: a US hyperscale campus moves to full build-out with the tenant funding generation, storage and transmission.
items.source: Entergy Arkansas news release 19 Oct 2026 (primary); DCD 20 Oct 2026

items.title: Denmark puts data centres last in line for constrained grid capacity as executive order 892 takes effect
items.summary: Denmark's executive order no. 892 on prioritising capacity and refusing connections under grid constraints, issued by the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Utilities on 9 October and published 15 October 2026, took effect on 19 October. It sets four priority categories for connection requests to the public electricity grid; data centres whose main purpose is network-based data processing, storage and related IT services sit in category 4, the lowest. Data centres needed for a critical societal function can qualify for category 1. When capacity is constrained, grid operators can refuse lower-priority requests that would displace higher-priority needs, and willingness to accept flexible connection terms is part of the assessment. Requests of 3 MW or more are handled in regional rounds held at least twice a year. This is a rationing rule, not a ban on new data centres. Country conversion: Danish AI and cloud campuses now queue behind households, electrification and storage wherever the grid is tight.
items.source: Bekendtgorelse nr. 892, Klima-, Energi- og Forsyningsministeriet, 9 Oct 2026, Lovtidende 15 Oct 2026 (primary); Digital Watch Observatory 19 Oct 2026

items.title: Israel's Electricity Authority backs a 200 MW cap per new data center and about 1,000 MW of new large data center connections after 27,000 MW of requests
items.summary: On the evening of 18 October 2026 Israel's Electricity Authority published the main points of new rules for connecting large data centers, as reported by Calcalist and other Israeli outlets. Each new data center would be capped at 200 MW. The Authority would allocate about 1,000 MW more to large data centers on top of roughly 2,000 MW already approved, about 3,000 MW in total or about 20% of projected 2030 national consumption; some outlets also report a further 300 MW reserved for defense and government needs. Grid operator Noga had received data center connection requests totalling 27,000 MW, about three times Israel's average consumption, and the Authority had frozen responses. Developers would post guarantees of NIS 2 million per requested MW (reported: half returned only once 60% of the capacity operates) and accept disconnection during extreme demand. Calcalist says requests for 500 MW and 1,100 MW sites would be blocked. The full decision goes to a three-week public consultation and may change before it takes effect. Country conversion: Israel is converting a 27 GW request queue into a capped, bonded allocation.
items.source: Calcalist / Ctech 19 Oct 2026; Sektor; The State of Israel 18 Oct 2026; Electricity Authority decision summary (full text pending consultation)

items.title: Singapore neocloud Aolani signs non-binding letters of intent for up to 500 MW of AI data centre capacity in Malaysia from 2H 2027
items.summary: On 19 October 2026 Aolani, a Singapore-founded neocloud, said it signed letters of intent to take up 500 MW of AI data centre capacity across multiple Malaysian sites, targeted to come online from the second half of 2027 and designed to Tier III. Aolani would supply the AI infrastructure, GPU deployment and operations; it projects committing up to 580 MW in Malaysia by 2027, up from about 80 MW committed in 2026, to serve hyperscalers, AI-native companies and Malaysian sovereign AI programmes. The release does not name the site owners, locations, GPU supplier or financing. The letters are non-binding and subject to definitive agreements. Country conversion: a demand-side LOI for Malaysian capacity, not yet a contract.
items.source: Aolani release via Media OutReach Newswire 19 Oct 2026 (primary); W.Media 20 Oct 2026

items.title: NextDC halts ASX trading over a delay to power supply at its M3 Melbourne data center and flags possible impact on FY27 guidance
items.summary: On 19 October 2026 NextDC (ASX: NXT) asked the ASX for an immediate trading halt so it could assess the impact of a delay to the supply of power at its M3 Melbourne data center in West Footscray, including on the FY27 guidance it has given the market. The request says the board had not yet met to consider the delay; the halt runs until NextDC makes an announcement or until normal trading on Wednesday 21 October. Bloomberg reports M3 is partially operating, with about 42 MW brought online during FY2026 and a further 165 MW under development. NextDC did not state the cause. Citi analysts Siraj Ahmed and Howard Suen wrote that the delay likely relates to distributor Jemena pausing work in September on 66 kV lines through residential streets after resident and council concerns, and estimated FY27 EBITDA could fall by up to A$25 million; that is an analyst attribution, not a company statement. AusNet says power demand from advanced data center proposals in Victoria exceeds the state's existing capacity. Country conversion: an operating Australian AI campus is gated by distribution lines, not tenant demand.
items.source: NextDC ASX trading halt request 19 Oct 2026 (primary, via ASX Market Announcement); Bloomberg via Energy Connects 19 Oct; AFR and Capital Brief 19 Oct

items.title: Microsoft exits its anchor deal at Nscale's Loughton, Essex AI data center after UK Power Networks pushes grid power into the 2030s
items.summary: Microsoft has ended its agreement to take capacity at Nscale's planned AI data center in Loughton, Essex, first reported by The Telegraph on 18 October 2026 and followed by the BBC, the Guardian, the FT and City AM. UK Power Networks had told Nscale the site would not get sufficient grid power until the early to mid 2030s, against a planned 2026 power date and 2027 opening, citing work needed on the wider transmission network. The project was announced in 2025 as the UK's largest AI supercomputer: Nscale pledged about GBP 2 billion, around 23,000 Nvidia GPUs were planned to serve Microsoft Azure, and Nscale has said the site could grow from 50 to 90 MW. Microsoft had said only last month that part of its US$30 billion UK investment would fund the Loughton supercomputer. A Microsoft spokesperson told City AM the decision 'relates to a single site' and that it remains committed to the partnership; Nscale said it remains committed to Loughton, is exploring alternative power sources and other UK sites, and that the grid issue has no impact on its other contracts. The two still work together in Norway, Portugal and the US. Country conversion: the UK's flagship AI compute site has lost its anchor tenant because of grid timing, not demand.
items.source: The Telegraph 18 Oct 2026 (first report); BBC 18-19 Oct; Guardian 18 Oct; City AM 19 Oct (Microsoft and Nscale statements); FT

items.title: Anthropic signs a 20-year lease for the first 95 MW of EverWind's planned 420 MW Point Tupper campus in Nova Scotia, its first data center deal in Canada
items.summary: On 16 October 2026 EverWind announced more than $10 billion of planned private investment at Point Tupper, Nova Scotia: more than $8 billion to develop, build, own and finance a data center campus and $2 billion for four onshore wind projects (Bear Lake, Windy Ridge, Kmtnuk, Upper Afton). The campus starts with a 95 MW phase in late 2027 and a 325 MW expansion targeted for 2028, subject to commercial, technical and regulatory conditions, for 420 MW at full build. EverWind's release names only a 'leading frontier AI developer' on a long-term lease; Anthropic confirmed in its own release the same day that it will lease the first phase for at least 20 years to power Claude models, and Reuters reported it as Anthropic's first Canadian data center agreement. EverWind says it will fund all connection, network upgrade and other system costs attributable to the project, add several hundred MWh of batteries, design the campus to cut grid draw when needed, and not connect the expansion until system studies and approvals are complete; existing grid supply serves phase 1 at first. Closed-loop cooling is estimated at about 100,000 litres of water a day for phase 1 and 500,000 at 420 MW. About 2,000 construction and 215 permanent jobs are projected; a Membertou-led First Nations consortium is negotiating an equity stake (CBC: 9%). Land clearing is underway. Country conversion: a frontier lab has signed a binding, multi-decade lease for Canadian capacity behind a developer-funded grid connection.
items.source: EverWind release via GlobeNewswire 16 Oct 2026 (primary); Anthropic release 16 Oct as reported by CBC News; Reuters and Canadian Press 16-17 Oct

items.title: NiSource GenCo signs a 20-year Microsoft energy agreement for northwest Indiana: ~1,100 MW new generation from 2028 plus 600 MW BESS, fully funded by the hyperscaler
items.summary: On 16 October 2026 NiSource Inc. announced a long-term energy agreement with Microsoft for its previously announced northwest Indiana data center campus. Under NiSource Generation Company LLC (GenCo), Microsoft is expected to begin taking electric service on a 20-year term starting in 2028. The GenCo-owned pool portfolio will increase by approximately 1,100 MW of new generation resources, and NIPSCO and GenCo will provide transmission and generation infrastructure; Microsoft fully funds all generation and transmission required to serve its load. In connection with the agreement, GenCo contracted 600 MW of battery storage under a long-term tolling agreement with an AGP Group affiliate, added to GenCo’s multi-customer pool. NiSource says expected NIPSCO electric customer savings over the life of data center contracts rise to about $1.75 billion (from $1.4 billion previously disclosed), as much as about $140 per customer annually. Additional operational and financial detail is slated for NiSource’s third-quarter earnings call. Country conversion: a named hyperscaler load in Indiana now sits behind customer-funded GenCo generation and storage rather than a standard residential-rate pass-through.

items.title: Uruguay and Solaria sign a strategic FTZ agreement for up to 500 MW of data-center campus capacity plus up to 350 MW solar (US$5.7B cited)
items.summary: On 14 October 2026 Uruguay’s President Yamandú Orsi signed a strategic agreement with Spain’s Solaria Energía y Medio Ambiente to develop a data-center technology campus of up to 500 MW under the free-trade-zone regime, together with up to 350 MW of solar PV on UTE land with a PPA envisaged for up to 40 years. Solaria will develop and operate the FTZ (land, infrastructure, services) and the electrical connection to Uruguay’s 500 kV grid. Development is phased: an initial 200 MW of data-center capacity (Canelones) then an additional 300 MW (San José), with solar concentrated in Florida. Uruguay’s Ministry of Industry, Energy and Mining cites a historic US$5.7 billion investment (about US$5.5 billion data centers and US$200 million solar), roughly 3,100 construction jobs in phase one (~2029) and about 1,500 permanent jobs at full operation. Binding contracts remain ahead (press coverage points to a May 2027 target). Country conversion: a sovereign-sponsored LatAm package of FTZ land, renewables, and transmission for operator tenants, not yet a named hyperscaler offtake.
items.source: MIEM Uruguay 14 Oct 2026; Solaria corporate release

items.title: EdgeConneX and Stockland launch a 50:50 Australia JV with 450 MW secured for Sydney and Melbourne hyperscale campuses
items.summary: On 14 October 2026 EdgeConneX announced a 50:50 joint venture with Stockland (ASX: SGP) to develop, own, and operate hyperscale data center campuses in Australia, starting with Sydney and Melbourne. The partners say they have secured 450 MW of power across the initial portfolio and are progressing additional power applications and planning. EdgeConneX appointed Chris Maher as Managing Director for Australia and joined Data Centres Australia as a principal member. Stockland’s earlier 3Q26 ASX operational update had already flagged contractual negotiations for the partnership and three existing sites with secured power totaling 450 MW. Country conversion: a new Australian sponsor platform enters with megawatts already secured rather than land-only optionality.

items.title: PJM files an executed study agreement at FERC to evaluate SB Energy's 10.37 GW Flagship AI campus in Pike County, Ohio under Ohio's State Agreement Approach
items.summary: On 13 October 2026 PJM Interconnection filed an executed Study Agreement (FERC Docket ER27-126-000, Rate Schedule No. 54, signed 25 September) with SB Energy affiliates SE DC DevCo, PORTS 2 Interconnect and Portsmouth Gas DevCo and AEP Ohio Transmission. PJM will study the Flagship Project at the former DOE Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio as one integrated load, generation and transmission package: an initial 800 MW (Mercury, new Monza 345 kV substation, served under the Ohio Power data center tariff) plus about 9,570 MW of additional load (Artemis, new Baku 765 kV substation), for 10,370 MW of firm NITS requested, and about 10,170 MW of gross new GE Vernova gas generation (7HA.2 combined cycle, 6F and aeroderivative units), phased through 2032, with three proposed 765 kV lines. SB Energy's development affiliate pays all study costs ($500,000 deposit, actual cost reimbursed); load flow and short circuit studies are expected within 60 days and stability within 120 days of data review. The filing names OpenAI as the data center tenant, alongside $40 million of SB Energy community benefits and $40 million from OpenAI. Acceptance would not approve any line, cost allocation or interconnection right; PUCO must sign an SAA agreement or issue a binding cost order within 120 days of PJM's final System Upgrade Report or the agreement terminates. Country conversion: a roughly 10 GW US AI campus now has a formal, developer-funded grid study path inside PJM, outside the normal interconnection queue.
items.source: PJM FERC filing ER27-126-000 (13 Oct 2026, primary); Utility Dive 14 Oct

items.title: NeoAI Cloud closes KRW 600 billion of financing for a 40 MW AI data center in Pohang, South Korea, with NHN Cloud pre-leasing half the IT load
items.summary: On 12 October 2026 NeoAI Cloud said it completed KRW 600 billion of financing for phase 1 of its Pohang AI data center in the Gwangmyeong industrial complex, North Gyeongsang Province: a KRW 450 billion project finance loan closed on 7 October and KRW 150 billion of equity. NeoAI Cloud and Singapore-based SC Capital Partners are the core equity investors, joined by North Gyeongsang Province, the government Regional Revitalization Investment Fund (its ninth project) and domestic lenders. Phase 1 is 40 MW of utility supply and 32 MW of IT load with liquid cooling for dense GPU clusters; power and the building permit are secured, Hyundai Engineering and Construction has been building since June 2026, and service launch is targeted for Q4 2027. NHN Cloud has committed to pre-lease 16 MW, half the IT capacity. A 260 MW phase 2 is in development. Country conversion: a financed, half-leased AI shell outside the Seoul metro, backed by public regional funds.
items.source: Asia Business Daily 12 Oct 2026; ETNews 12 Oct 2026 (company release)

items.title: CapitaLand India Trust launches CapitaLand Data Centre Chennai 01: 34 MW IT, 53 MW gross, about US$203 million, completion by end 2026
items.summary: On 15 October 2026 CapitaLand India Trust (CLINT) launched CapitaLand Data Centre Chennai 01 in Ambattur, Chennai, its first data center in Tamil Nadu, with Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay. The facility represents about INR 19.4 billion (US$203.2 million) of investment, will have 53 MW of gross power capacity and 34 MW of IT capacity across 13 data halls when completed by the end of 2026, and is designed for high-density computing including liquid cooling. It is jointly held by CLINT and CapitaLand India Data Centre Fund. CLINT's Navi Mumbai data center is fully leased to a global hyperscaler; no tenant is named for Chennai. Country conversion: another sponsor-built, near-complete shell in India's second data center corridor, launched at head-of-state level.
items.source: The Business Times 15 Oct 2026; The Hindu BusinessLine 15 Oct

items.title: AEP plans about $4 billion for a 702 MW Bloom fuel cell plant near Cheyenne, Wyoming under a 20-year Google PPA
items.summary: On 14 October 2026 American Electric Power (Nasdaq: AEP) said it plans to invest about $4 billion in a new 702 MW fuel cell generation project near Cheyenne, Wyoming, selling the output to Google under a 20-year power purchase agreement. The project company, Cheyenne Fuel Cell, LLC, is about 92% owned and controlled by AEP and nearly 8% by funds advised by Basalt Infrastructure Partners. The plant uses Bloom Energy fuel cells, generates power without combustion of natural gas, and includes plans to integrate carbon capture. Construction is planned to start in 2026, with full operation expected by the end of 2028. AEP says the plant supports Google's growing energy needs in the greater Cheyenne area and follows the Google and Black Hills Corp. agreements effective 30 September (already on the Wire). Country conversion: a named hyperscaler now has a second, utility-financed firm generation source for its Wyoming load, built outside AEP's traditional service territory.

items.title: Fermi discloses a binding 15-year, $6.5 billion TensorWave lease for 222 MW at Project Matador, Texas, backed by AMD credit support
items.summary: On 14 October 2026 Fermi Inc. (Nasdaq/LSE: FRMI) furnished an 8-K fact sheet describing a binding 15-year phase one lease with TensorWave at Project Matador in Carson County, Texas: 222 MW of total power capacity including 156 MW of critical IT capacity, $6.5 billion of contracted revenue over the initial term, two 5-year renewal options and 2.5% annual escalators. Fermi develops, builds and delivers turnkey; TensorWave takes occupancy in phases from Q4 2027, completing in early 2028. Fermi cites power capex of $3M to $4M per MW of total power capacity and turnkey data center capex of $10M to $12M per MW of critical IT, and an estimated phase one project-level NOI margin of about 75% to 80% (non-GAAP). AMD signed credit support on 13 October; per the filing it begins only after construction is complete and rent starts on the final delivery phase, and it ends early if TensorWave or its guarantor holds an investment-grade rating for 12 consecutive months. Project financing is not yet closed. Country conversion: the first named, priced tenant lease on a behind-the-meter Texas Panhandle AI campus, with a chipmaker balance sheet behind it.
items.source: Fermi 8-K (Item 7.01, Exhibit 99.1 TensorWave fact sheet) 14 Oct 2026; Fermi x AMD credit support release (Access Newswire) 13 Oct

items.title: Mason County, Kentucky approves a community benefits agreement with Meta for a hyperscale data center on more than 2,000 zoned acres
items.summary: On 13 October 2026 the Mason County Fiscal Court (Maysville, Kentucky) voted unanimously to approve a resolution and community benefits agreement for a hyperscale data center, and Judge-Executive Owen McNeill named Meta as the developer. More than 2,000 acres have been zoned for the project. Reported figures differ: county attorney Jim Parsons put the initial investment at about $15 billion (WKYT), while the agreement as reported by the Ledger Independent and Mason County Post commits $10 billion of capital investment, with about $800 billion of Industrial Revenue Bonds associated with a 40-year, multi-phase plan (about $10 billion per phase). Other terms include more than 2,000 construction jobs, at least 400 full-time jobs, about $115 million of road, water and sewer improvements, and a $15 million public safety fee. Construction of the first phase is expected within three years. Meta's statement calls it a potential project and says it will pay the full cost of the power it uses. No MW, utility or energization date is disclosed. Country conversion: a named hyperscaler secures local approval for a multi-phase Kentucky campus.
items.source: WKYT 13 Oct 2026; Mason County Post 13 Oct (citing Ledger Independent) with Meta statement

items.title: Bitdeer AI locks an 8-year, 60 MW A103 AI Cloud facility at its Cyberjaya, Malaysia campus
items.summary: On 12 October 2026 Bitdeer AI (Bitdeer Technologies Group, NASDAQ: BTDR) announced an 8-year data center services agreement for A103, a 60 MW (critical IT load) AI Cloud facility on the same Cyberjaya, Malaysia campus as A101 and A102. A103 is designed for liquid-cooled, rack-scale NVIDIA systems including the next-generation Vera Rubin platform, with energization expected in Q1 2028. With A103, the Cyberjaya campus is expected to reach about 71.5 MW, and Bitdeer AI's secured AI Cloud capacity (owned or under an executed DCA) rises to about 333.5 MW across Malaysia, Norway and the United States, or about 95% of its up-to-350 MW target for delivery by Q1 2028. An earlier 8 Oct GlobeNewswire version of the same headline was withdrawn the same day (notice to disregard). The company discloses no offtake commitments for A103 capacity as of the release. Country conversion: Malaysia gains another executed 60 MW AI Cloud shell on an existing campus that already has power, liquid cooling and network in place.
items.source: Bitdeer / GlobeNewswire 12 Oct (Markets Insider syndication); Seeking Alpha 12 Oct; Oct 8 disregard notice on GlobeNewswire

items.title: FERC accepts PJM's 50 MW Large Load definition and registry, rejects the interim curtailment service for new large loads
items.summary: On 9 October 2026 FERC issued its order in Docket ER26-3515 (197 FERC 61,019) accepting PJM Interconnection's definition of a Large Load, end-use load with a cumulative peak of 50 MW or more at a single electrical site (affiliated facilities within a one-mile radius count as one site), and a Large Load Registry under which load-serving entities report each large load's location, peak, ramp schedule and backup generation, effective 12 October 2026. FERC rejected the rest of PJM's 13 August filing as one package: the Interim Resource Adequacy Service that could have curtailed new large loads lacking new capacity in emergencies, the Bring Your Own New Capacity rules, and the plan to drop uncovered new large load from the capacity demand curve from the 2029/2030 delivery year. FERC said parts of the tariff appeared to intrude on retail rate regulation. PJM must make a compliance filing within 30 days; Commissioner Rosner concurred separately. No megawatt is added: PJM says its 2028/2029 auction cleared about 6.8 GW short of the reliability requirement. Country conversion: the largest US grid now tracks every 50 MW data center site, but new AI load will not face mandatory early curtailment for now.
items.source: FERC eLibrary accession 20261009-3055 (Order, ER26-3515-000); Headwaters Wire 9 Oct; The Duck Curve 10 Oct

items.title: Sesterce plans a EUR 10bn-plus AI campus at the former Kaipola paper mill in Jamsa, Finland: 200 MW first phase, 600 MW second, anchor customer signed
items.summary: On 8 October 2026 French AI infrastructure company Sesterce announced a planned investment of over EUR 10 billion in a Sesterce Campus at the former Kaipola paper mill in Jamsa, Central Finland. The first phase, with works planned to start in 2026, is 200 MW, rising to 600 MW in a second phase; Sesterce aims for more than 1 GW of AI capacity in Finland over time. Sesterce says it already has an anchor customer; its CEO told Yle the investment decision is made and a contract is signed with one of the two leading AI labs, without naming it or the financial backers. Grid operator Elenia says the site's high-voltage connection is a solid foundation for the first phase. Sesterce does not yet own the site (seller Kaipola Green Port says talks are advanced), and Jamsa notes permits are still outstanding. Country conversion: a second large AI campus with a signed frontier-lab anchor lands in Finland in the same week as Applied Digital's Finnish power access.
items.source: Sesterce newsroom 8 Oct; Yle News 8 Oct (CEO confirmation of signed client); City of Jamsa release

items.title: Indiana regulators approve AES Indiana's large-load plan to serve Google's 390 MW Monrovia data center
items.summary: On 7 October 2026 the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission unanimously approved AES Indiana's large-load growth plan supporting Google's data center in Morgan County (Monrovia), the first data center filed under Indiana's 2025 large-load law (HEA 1007). The project includes solar, two battery storage systems and lines to serve a 390 MW Google facility; WFYI reports total project cost of $737.3 million and AES's estimated infrastructure investment of $1.3 billion. AES says Google's rates cover 100% of energy, infrastructure, transmission and generation costs, with an 80% minimum demand obligation and a contract of at least 15 years; the order still lets $73.8 million of network upgrades go into transmission rate base, which the Citizens Action Coalition opposed. AES estimates about $770 million in customer savings. Country conversion: a state commission converts a 390 MW hyperscale load into an approved, ratepayer-ring-fenced utility build in MISO.
items.source: AES Indiana release 7 Oct; WFYI 12 Oct; Indianapolis Business Journal

items.title: Applied Digital secures access to up to 1 GW of potential power in Finland for its first non-US AI Factory campus
items.summary: On 6 October 2026 Applied Digital (Nasdaq: APLD) said it entered an agreement giving it access to up to 1 GW of potential power capacity in Finland, its first development opportunity outside the United States. The company plans a large-scale AI Factory campus that could scale to as much as 1 GW, with initial power availability anticipated beginning in 2028. It has begun marketing the site and says it is in discussions with leading global hyperscale customers. The release does not name the counterparty, exact site, utility, financing, construction schedule, or a committed tenant. Near-term execution remains centered on the US portfolio. Country conversion: a US AI-campus developer locks Nordic power access for a first international build.
items.source: Applied Digital IR via GlobeNewswire; Yahoo Finance; Grid and Silicon

items.title: DarkHorse signs up to 50 MW with Hopkinsville Electric System for a new Kentucky superintelligence factory
items.summary: On 6 October 2026 DarkHorse Technologies (Nasdaq: DRK) said its subsidiary Pennyrile Holdings signed a power contract with the Electric Plant Board of Hopkinsville, Kentucky (Hopkinsville Electric System) for up to 50 MW for a new superintelligence factory, doubling DarkHorse contracted power in the TVA region to about 100 MW. DarkHorse will fund in full a new 65 MW HES-owned substation on TVA 161 kV, taking 50 MW; about 15 MW is for existing HES customers. The power contract has a ten-year initial term from commencement with automatic five-year renewals. Service remains subject to an eighteen-month permit contingency, utility construction, and other conditions; TVA has approved capacity to serve the project. No end customer is named. Country conversion: contracted municipal utility power for a new US AI campus in Kentucky.
items.source: DarkHorse release via Newsfile; Nasdaq syndication; Christian County Now

items.title: CoreWeave enters India as sole tenant of a 240 MW AdaniConneX campus in Navi Mumbai, with Vera Rubin planned
items.summary: On 7 October 2026 CoreWeave (Nasdaq: CRWV) announced its entry into India through a collaboration with AdaniConneX, the 50:50 Adani Enterprises and EdgeConneX joint venture. CoreWeave plans to take 240 MW of data center capacity across three 80 MW buildings at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai as sole tenant, with an option to expand by up to another 240 MW at the campus. It plans to deploy the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, with direct liquid cooling and a non-evaporative chilled water system. The first phase is expected to be available in mid-2028, with more capacity in phases. CoreWeave also plans an India office and local hiring. The release uses plan language, gives no investment figure and names no end customer. Country conversion: a top US neocloud commits to its first Indian campus at hyperscale size.
items.source: CoreWeave release via Business Wire; NDTV Profit; The Next Web

items.title: Black Hills signs definitive agreements through 2048 to serve Google's planned Cheyenne, Wyoming data center with a 2.7 GW resource mix
items.summary: On 6 October 2026 Black Hills Corp. (NYSE: BKH) said it signed definitive agreements, effective 30 September 2026 with terms through 2048, to serve a planned Google data center in Cheyenne, Wyoming. The project is to be served by a total resource mix of 2.7 GW including reserve margins: up to 590 MW of grid-connected service, mostly from 564 MW of new company-owned natural gas generation at the Cheyenne Prairie Generating Station ($1.8 billion, built 2027 to 2029), plus about 2.1 GW of Wyoming-based third-party contracted resources managed through a private microgrid. Energy service is planned to start in late 2027 and ramp to peak load in 2030. Google has advanced $399 million, refundable, for long-lead equipment and bears all costs of serving the site under the agreements. Transmission filings are still pending at the Wyoming PSC, and the Google campus itself is described as planned. Country conversion: a hyperscaler locks in dedicated multi-GW power for a new US campus.
items.source: Black Hills Corp. release via GlobeNewswire; Form 8-K

items.title: TeraWulf doubles contracted power at its Muskie campus in eastern Kentucky to 1 GW and pulls the second 500 MW into 2029
items.summary: On 5 October 2026 TeraWulf (Nasdaq: WULF) said it executed an amended and restated electric service agreement with Kentucky Power, an AEP company, raising contracted capacity at its Muskie Data Campus in eastern Kentucky from 500 MW to 1 GW. The second 500 MW phase moves from 2030 to 2029, subject to Kentucky Public Service Commission approval and Kentucky Power's construction schedule; the first 500 MW phase still targets a 2028 ramp. Kentucky Power is building a 765 kV / 345 kV substation for the site and says the agreement carries about $100 million in customer benefits. TeraWulf says it may take the campus toward 2 GW over time. No tenant is named for Muskie. Country conversion: a US AI campus doubles its contracted utility power ahead of a signed tenant.
items.source: TeraWulf release via GlobeNewswire; Form 8-K; Kentucky Power release; ENR

items.title: Google signs 20-year PPA for 890 MW of new nuclear uprate capacity plus a 15-year, 2,700 MW supply deal with Constellation in PJM
items.summary: On 6 October 2026 Google and Constellation Energy announced a 20-year power purchase agreement that funds uprates at 11 Constellation nuclear units in Illinois, Pennsylvania and New Jersey, adding 890 MW of new capacity to the PJM grid, with the first uprate expected by 2028 and more than $4.3 billion of Constellation investment. The companies also signed a 15-year energy supply agreement for a further 2,700 MW from Constellation's PJM fleet, about 3,590 MW in total per CNBC. The release frames the deal as a response to PJM's Bring Your Own Power proposal and includes demand-response and load-shaping terms. Power stays on the PJM grid; the release does not name which Google data centers it serves. Country conversion: a hyperscaler pre-funds new firm generation for its PJM load rather than waiting on new interconnection.
items.source: Constellation Energy and Google joint release; CNBC

items.title: Applied Digital brings another 75 MW online at Polaris Forge 1 in North Dakota, taking the campus to 250 MW operational
items.summary: On 2 October 2026 Applied Digital (Nasdaq: APLD) said it reached Ready for Service on the second phase of Building 2 at its Polaris Forge 1 campus in Ellendale, North Dakota, delivering 75 MW of critical IT load across three 25 MW data halls. That completes Building 2 at 150 MW and brings fully operational critical IT at the campus to 250 MW, against 400 MW contracted at full buildout. The release says the campus is fully leased but does not name the tenant in this announcement; trade press (The Latent) describes it as CoreWeave-leased. Country conversion: contracted US AI capacity becomes energized, usable capacity.

items.title: JERA, Dell and RHAELM sign MoU for national-scale AI infrastructure in Japan, starting with a 400 MW behind-the-meter campus at Chiba
items.summary: On 1 October 2026 JERA, Japan's largest power generator, Dell Technologies and London-based RHAELM signed a memorandum of understanding to build a standardized model for AI infrastructure in Japan. The first project is at JERA's Chiba Thermal Power Station, supported by up to 400 MW of behind-the-meter power, with total capital deployment expected to exceed US$15 billion (2.3 trillion yen) across land, power, construction and AI compute, and operations targeted around 2028. Apollo intends to serve as RHAELM's strategic investment and financing partner, and Dell supplies the rack-scale compute standard. JERA and RHAELM plan to explore more JERA sites toward multi-gigawatt capacity in the 2030s. This is an MoU, not a final investment decision, and no offtake customer is named. Country conversion: Japan's dominant generator commits an operating plant site and power to a named AI campus.
items.source: JERA press release; RHAELM release; Data Center Dynamics

items.title: AM Intelligence places firm orders for 20,000 more NVIDIA Rubin GPUs for India and Malaysia (~70 MW, Q2 2027)
items.summary: On 5 October 2026 AM Intelligence (AMI), the AI infrastructure platform set up by Greenko's promoters, announced two further firm and binding orders for 20,000 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, to be deployed as Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems across Malaysia and India, totalling about 70 MW with delivery scheduled for Q2 2027. With the 25 August order for 9,000 Rubin GPUs at its first Hyderabad AI factory, AMI's committed total is about 29,000 Rubin GPUs and close to 100 MW. AMI says it plans to bring a further 300 MW to market over the next 15 months with capex of more than $20 billion, on top of $6 billion already committed for the initial ~100 MW; NVIDIA's Asia South managing director is quoted in the statement. The split of the 70 MW between India and Malaysia and the site locations are not disclosed. Company statement carried by tele.net, BusinessLine and Times of India; no separate NVIDIA release found.
items.source: AM Intelligence statement via tele.net; The Hindu BusinessLine

items.title: Nebius signs binding 12-year deal for 50 MW critical IT at AIB Data Centers' southeastern US site
items.summary: On 30 September 2026 AIB Data Centers (NYSE American: AIB) announced that a wholly owned subsidiary entered a binding Master Colocation Services Agreement with Nebius (Nasdaq: NBIS) for 50 MW of critical IT capacity at AIB's facility in the southeastern United States, with an initial 12-year term and optional renewals; the release was furnished on Form 8-K. AIB expects Nebius prepayments under the initial term, plus project-level debt and preferred equity, to fund a substantial portion of initial development cost. Capacity is backed by AIB's previously announced 15-year Electric Service Agreement for 65 MW of utility load requiring no significant additional electrical upgrades, and will be delivered in two data halls. The state and contract value are not disclosed in the release; trade press (Baxtel, 2 Oct) reports the first hall within about 10 months and the second within about 14 months, not stated in the primary. Country conversion: a named neocloud tenant converts powered US capacity into long-term contracted MW with customer prepayment financing.
items.source: AIB Data Centers via GlobeNewswire; Form 8-K

items.title: Bitdeer AI contracts >70% offtake on 21.7 MW Johor A201 ahead of Q1 2027 energization
items.summary: On 29 September 2026 Bitdeer AI (Bitdeer Technologies Group, Nasdaq: BTDR) announced off-take commitments covering more than 70% of approximately 21.7 MW at its A201 liquid-cooled AI Cloud facility in Johor Bahru, Malaysia, ahead of planned energization in Q1 2027. Expected five-year site revenue exceeds $1.7 billion; company AI Cloud revenue backlog is stated at about $2.9 billion. A201 is purpose-built for NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 with a portion of racks designed for Vera Rubin; Bitdeer says it procured more than 100 GB300 NVL72 racks from an unaffiliated supplier. Together with A202, the Johor campus path is 86.8 MW toward a company target of up to 350 MW AI Cloud capacity by Q1 2028. Customer names are not disclosed. Country conversion: Malaysia gains a named MW AI Cloud campus with majority contracted offtake before energization (distinct from the prior Firmus/OpenAI Malaysia factory Wire).

items.title: RWE signs 433 MW West Texas VPPA with Oracle for AI data-center power
items.summary: On 17 September 2026 RWE Americas announced a virtual power purchase agreement with Oracle for 433 MW from existing Panther Creek I, II and III wind farms in Sterling, Howard and Glasscock counties (West Texas). RWE says the VPPA is part of Oracle’s broader Texas power portfolio totaling more than 1.7 GW supporting the ERCOT grid for Oracle data-center operations. Country conversion: a named hyperscaler locks another hundreds-of-MW renewable hedge onto Texas generation that already exists — firming Oracle’s Texas AI load path without waiting on new interconnect alone.

items.title: CleanSpark names Meta (Anviran) as 175 MW Sandersville AI tenant; proposes $2.227B notes
items.summary: On 17 September 2026 CleanSpark disclosed in investor materials accompanying an SEC filing that Anviran LLC — tenant on its 175 MW Sandersville, Georgia campus under a previously announced 20-year triple-net lease (~$6.6B expected revenue over the initial term) — is a wholly owned Meta Platforms subsidiary, with Meta guaranteeing rent and opex. Same day CleanSpark PR Newswire: subsidiary CSDC Finance I proposes $2.227B senior secured notes due 2031 to finish Sandersville (offering not closed; market conditions). Rent commencement targeted Q4 2027. Country conversion: Georgia AI campus moves from unnamed IG tenant to named Meta + a public $2.2B construction finance pitch.
items.source: CleanSpark PR Newswire + SEC investor materials (via reporting)

items.title: Anthropic signs first Australia lease at Zerra Western Downs (path to 2.16 GW peak)
items.summary: On 16 September 2026, Queensland Premier David Crisafulli announced in Parliament that Anthropic signed its first Australian data-centre lease as anchor tenant at Singapore developer Zerra DC’s proposed Western Downs Digital Park near Dalby (~250 km from Brisbane). Planning docs put IT capacity at ~1.44 GW across four halls and peak grid draw about 2.16 GW at full build; Reuters (sources) and ABC report first use targeted 2027 for inference (not training), closed-loop/air-cooled design, and FIRB + Western Downs Regional Council approvals still outstanding. Anthropic and Zerra declined comment to Reuters. Country conversion: Australia gets a named frontier-lab lease on a GW-class campus — still FIRB/council/power gated, not energization.
items.corroboration: Reuters Sydney 16 Sep (anonymous sources; Anthropic/Zerra no comment). Premier Crisafulli Parliament remarks same day (ABC / Brisbane Times / Guardian). techAU 17 Sep on Zerra DA (lodged 17 Aug) and 1.44 GW IT / 2.16 GW peak figures from planning docs.

items.title: Bell × Saskatchewan MOU: up to +900 MW AI Fabric (path to 1.2 GW hub)
items.summary: On 14 September 2026 Bell Canada and the Government of Saskatchewan announced a non-binding memorandum of understanding to expand Bell AI Fabric with phased development of up to 900 MW of additional capacity — creating a path to a 1.2 GW Canadian AI infrastructure hub in the province (Saskatchewan release: retain original 300 MW from the provincial grid plus up to 900 MW under Bring Your Own Power / partner natural-gas generation). Bell PR: closed-loop cooling (no municipal water); HQ of Bell AI Fabric national ecosystem in Saskatchewan; full-buildout capital including DC, tenant compute and related generation could exceed $50 billion; subject to customer commitments, commercial agreements, permits and environmental assessments. Country conversion: Canada gets a named provincial GW-path print with BYOP power — still MOU-gated, not a FID.
items.source: Bell Canada / CNW; Government of Saskatchewan
items.corroboration: Primary Bell CNW 14 Sep 16:30 ET + Saskatchewan government release same day (1.2 GW path = 300 MW grid + ≤900 MW BYOP). Data Center News Canada; ConstructConnect/Canadian Press 15 Sep on Carney/Moe summit framing.

items.title: ERCOT issues State & Community Impact RFI for Batch Zero / medium data centers (due Oct 12)
